ai.description: This small frog reaches 20–25 mm. It is brownish-grey with a dark interorbital bar and granular skin. A distinctive white spot is present on the snout, and the belly is creamy white.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes shillongensis* is best distinguished by the distinct, dark-brown, inverted V-shaped marking on its back, which is absent in most other regional bush frogs.
ai.habitat: The Shillong Bush Frog inhabits high-altitude subtropical broadleaf forests and shrublands in the Meghalaya hills, typically at elevations between 1,500 and 1,900 meters.
ai.behavior: The Shillong Bush Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the dense foliage of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes shillongensis* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in moist terrestrial sites.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Shillong Bush Frog is endemic to the Khasi Hills in Meghalaya, India, typically inhabiting high-altitude forest areas above 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Shillong Bush Frog emits a series of high-pitched, insect-like "tink-tink" notes, typically heard from dense vegetation within its humid forest habitat.
